content.text:
I found one phase: TiVO4 (mp-755748). Fitting it alone gave R = 0.78, much better than any other candidate.

1. **Peak positions.** The strongest peak is at about 25.25°. Smaller peaks sit near 36.6°, 37.1° (23) and a broad bump around 38.4°. Further strong peaks have intensities of about 31, 19 and 16, plus doublets at higher angle. That set matches an anatase-type (TiO2-like) tetragonal lattice.
2. **Matching candidate.** Of the nine, only TiVO4 (space group 119) has that structure. Its cell is a ≈ c ≈ 3.79 Å with a long axis of 9.69 Å, close to anatase.
3. **Single-phase fits.** I fitted seven of the nine candidates on their own. Six of them (BaHfO3, Ba2EuNbO6, Bi2O3, DyFeO3, SrFeO3 and Al3Bi(BO3)4) all had R between 0.98 and 1.06. Their residuals were essentially the full observed pattern, and none could reproduce the 25.25° peak. I did not fit VReO4 or AlAuO2.
4. **TiVO4 residual.** After the TiVO4 fit, what is left consists only of paired positive and negative wiggles at the TiVO4 peak positions. The largest is about ±24 at the main peak. That shape points to small mismatches in peak position or shape, not to a missing phase. I found no peaks left over at new positions, so I don't see evidence of a second phase.

I did not run a two-phase fit. The confidence below allows for that, and for the wiggles at the main peak.

{"present": ["mp-755748"], "confidence": 0.85, "note": "All observed peaks (25.25, 37.1, ~48, ~54/55 deg etc.) match the anatase-type TiVO4 pattern, and its fit leaves only derivative-shaped mismatch wiggles with no peaks at new positions, so no second phase is indicated."}
